newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland 96/97 white sugar output seen at 2.2 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Poland 96/97 white sugar output seen at 2.2 mln T.

text.p: Poland will produce a record of 2.2 to 2.25 million tonnes of white sugar in the 1996/1997 season against 1.58 million tonnes in 1995/1996, the head of the Sugar Council grouping sugar refineries said on Tuesday.
Ryszard Sugier told Reuters the amount of sugar that could be extracted from beets this year was one percentage point higher than last year at 13 percent.
"We expect to produce 2.2 to 2.25 million tonnes of sugar in this sugar campaign. By December 10 refineries had produced 1.86 million tonnes of white sugar," Sugier said.
Earlier estimates put this year's sugar production at 2.1 million tonnes.
High production has prompted the government to increase domestic sugar sales, the so-called A quota, by 130,000 tonnes to 1.63 million this year.
The export, B quota is at 122,900 tonnes in 1996 and 118,300 tonnes in 1997.
The rest of the sugar produced is encompassed by the so-called C quota, which will have to be sold without any subsidies, probably at a loss, on a saturated market.
In November the government said part of the C quota could be bought for state reserves.
